title: Become Superhuman: Way of the Ü
summary: Closing his Nietzsche self-improvement arc, NH presents 'white pills' drawn from Beyond Good and Evil as uncomfortable truths that invite struggle on the path to the Übermensch. He argues masculinity is mostly internal work, that endurance beats intensity, that the group will resist your improvement, and that lifting is an external practice that supports the inner transformation.
claims: A true white pill is an uncomfortable truth that pushes you to strive; any truth that comforts you into staying the same is a black or blue pill
The same harsh truth becomes a black pill or a white pill depending on whether the receiver treats it as a challenge
Masculinity is mostly internal; muscle and other outward signs are only the visible tip of the iceberg, and modern men over-focus on appearance
Duration of effort beats intensity: someone training super intensely once every 15 days will be outdone by someone training semi-intensely three times a week
Past the newbie phase gains stop being immediate; only those who keep putting in effort without immediate payback get the reward
Pleasure that comes without effort is worthless and chasing it leads to ruin; a healthy man accepts and seeks struggle
Perfection does not exist: reaching an ideal only reveals new goalposts, so a man's development only ends when he dies
Most of a man's work is inner exploration and introspection, and you are never done discovering yourself
Wealth, cars and women are external results of inner work like confidence and self-reliance, not worthy progress in themselves; his philosophy is anti-materialistic
Resenting nature for bad genetics or a poor background is a pathological mindset that ends in self-hatred and stagnation
When he started lifting he treated training as a duty or punishment, which led to injury and resentment; once he saw it as a hobby and passion the gains came back and he enjoyed it
Do not take yourself too seriously; seriousness is a shield to hide weaknesses, and you must accept your flaws before you can fix them
Hold to your principles and dreams even against good counterarguments; if someone can talk you out of a dream, you never had one
Expect disapproval from the group when you improve: people who won't work will work to pull you down, and those around you are the biggest killer of men's development
People who had no problem with him started mocking his efforts and calling him vain once he began improving, because he reflected their own inaction back at them
A man becomes a man outside the group; historical rites of passage had him face a hard challenge alone, and taboo ideas deserve to be tested
Praise breeds stagnation while blame drives growth; anyone not progressing is actively regressing
Think less and act more; overthinking breeds anxiety and inaction
Lifting is a good path toward the Übermensch because it is an external, repeated action that builds habits and facilitates internal work, though it is not enough alone
Masculinity marketing resurrects a corpse for profit; real masculinity is internal work that is free
Self-improvement that turns you into a clone of someone else's mold is not self-improvement; the goal is becoming the person you always wanted to be
